mechanism: schema-GATED directional disambiguation (entity,direction -> unique process via the hand-KB consumes/produces/moves structure) + anchor-gated NEW-entity extension; NOT a fade test

fairness.can_fail: HARD_FAIL if resolvable-case accuracy <= schema-blind 0.72, or resolvable fraction tiny, or extension wrong

design_gate.note: resolvable-case tag accuracy + extension correctness hand-checked by operator

design_gate_result.dominant_resolvable_error: distinctive schema entity appearing in a NON-process context: oil PUMPED/transported (logistics != hydrocarbon FORMATION); 'gas' from chemistry/greenhouse/volcanic/fuel (!= natural-gas formation); 'energy MOVED' in ecosystems/ocean-waves/chemistry (!= electricity generation); 'nutrient MOVED' in plants/oceans (!= digestion); food from chemosynthesis/cooking (!= photosynthesis). The schema assigns the process by the entity's schema-ROLE, but the entity recurs in OTHER real-world contexts.
design_gate_result.extension_failure_mode: co-occurrence over-binding: the anchor gates EVERY new entity in the sentence to the anchor's process, but most co-occurring new entities (ocean/atom/world/engine/panel/lactose/molecule/product) are UNRELATED to the anchor's process -> 8/10 wrong.

final_verdict_msg: HARD_FAIL_schema_gated_extension_fundamentally_limited [NO LLM, no-leak DEV-never-read, schema=blind-authored seed, can-fail]. SCHEMA-GATED directional disambiguation MODESTLY beats the schema-blind baseline on RESOLVABLE cases: accuracy=0.7833 (94/120) > 0.72 baseline, but BELOW the 0.85 target. HOWEVER the architecture's reading-extension is FUNDAMENTALLY LIMITED: only 18% of reads are schema-resolvable-direct (unique entity-direction); 22% are SHARED-AMBIGUOUS (schema can't disambiguate CO2/oxygen/water even WITH direction) and 53% are entirely NEW entities not in the schema. New-entity EXTENSION gated only 10 facts and is WRONG (0.2=2/10 correct) -- co-occurrence over-binding (ocean/atom/world/engine bound to an unrelated anchor process). CONCLUSION: schema-gated DISAMBIGUATION is a valid, modestly-better-than-blind mechanism on the ~18% of reads whose distinctive entity-direction is schema-unique AND in-context, but it is NOT a viable reading-EXTENSION engine: it cannot disambiguate the 75% shared/new majority, and its new-entity extension over-binds. The schema-gated conclusion is PARTLY confirmed (accurate disambiguation on distinctive entities) and PARTLY WRONG (reading-extension is fundamentally limited by entity-direction sharing + co-occurrence over-binding). The seed must permanently carry the shared/new majority; reading extends only the narrow schema-unique-in-context slice.
